summary.text: A 61-year-old woman with a history of obesity and hypertension was registered at a university hospital in December 2010 with a three-month history of dizziness, precordial pain and adynamia, a 5.5 kg weight loss and fever. Examination showed pallor and rare petechiae without palpable lymph nodes. Hemoglobin was 5.5 g/dl, platelet count 25 x 10^(3)/µl and leukocyte count 19.58 x 10^(3)/µl, and serological tests were negative.

Bone marrow immunophenotypic analyses showed 23% blasts, with CD34, HLADR and CD33 positivity and negativity for CD7, CD19, CD10, CD117, CD36 and CD15, characterizing acute myeloid leukemia, FAB classification M4.

She received one cycle of cytarabine and daunorubicin to induce remission and four consolidation cycles of cytarabine, and hematological remission followed one month after the first cycle. She relapsed in August 2011, when a myelogram showed blasts and immunophenotyping showed 71.2% positive blasts. Molecular analysis was positive for AML-ETO, and GTG banding and FISH showed a complex karyotype including ring chromosome 11.
A new conditioning regimen (FLAG) was started, but she died of septic shock in September 2011, 293 days after diagnosis.
